title: Number of Islands
statement: Given an m x n 2D binary grid which represents a map of 1s (land) and 0s (water), return the number of islands.
hints: Iterate over every cell (r, c) in the grid.
When you find a land cell (1), increment islands count and start a DFS flood fill.
Mark visited land cells as 0 so they are not counted again.

solutions.title: DFS Flood Fill
solutions.complexity: Time: O(R * C) | Space: O(R * C)

solutions.title: BFS Queue Flood Fill
solutions.complexity: Time: O(R * C) | Space: O(min(R, C))

editorial.approach: Scan the 2D grid cell by cell. Whenever an unvisited land cell '1' is encountered, increment the island counter and launch a BFS or DFS flood-fill from that coordinate. The flood-fill traverses all orthogonally connected land cells, marking them as visited (or flipping them in-place to '0') to ensure no cell is counted twice.
editorial.why_optimal: Every cell is inspected and marked at most once, yielding optimal O(M * N) time and O(min(M, N)) queue space for BFS or O(M * N) recursion depth for DFS.
editorial.pitfalls: Forgetting to mark cells as visited before pushing them to a BFS queue, causing duplicate insertions and queue memory blowup. Diagonal connections are not islands (only 4-directional moves allowed).
